item.title: Bonaire’s coral reef is disappearing, researchers warn
item.description:
Bonaire’s coral reef is disappearing, researchers warn

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The coral reef around Bonaire has fallen to about 5% of the seabed, down from more than 60% fifty years ago, researchers told broadcaster NOS on Monday.

The figures come from fieldwork on the Dutch Caribbean island that has not yet been published and which the researchers describe as a first analysis. A Wageningen Marine Research report published last year put average coral cover on Bonaire at under 10% and said algae now dominate the reefs.

The reef is central to a climate case Greenpeace Nederland brought against the Dutch state. Research behind that case found the coral helps shield Bonaire from flooding and that part of the island will be lost as sea levels rise.

The Hague district court ruled in January that Dutch climate policy breached the human rights of Bonaire’s residents and treated them unequally with people in the European Netherlands.

It gave ministers six months to quantify how much greenhouse gas the country can still emit, 18 months to turn that into binding targets, and until 2030 to produce a climate adaptation plan for the island.

The cabinet is appealing but remains bound by the judgment.

Coral researcher Erik Meesters of Wageningen University and Research said warming seawater was the main cause, worsened by a severe El Niño, and that higher temperatures also made coral more prone to disease.

Fast-growing species are surviving, he said, but the large reef-building corals that can reach ten metres are disappearing.

Bonaire’s economy depends heavily on diving tourism. The organisation Reef Renewal said it has planted 20,000 pieces of new coral around the island, while acknowledging the scale is not enough to solve the problem.

item.title: Ferries cancelled as rivers drop to record low levels in drought
item.description:
Ferries cancelled as rivers drop to record low levels in drought

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Several ferries across the Waal and IJssel rivers in Gelderland have been cancelled after the major Dutch rivers dropped to historically low levels in July.

The service across the Pannerdensch Kanaal, near where the Rhine flows into the Waal, between Doornenburg and Pannerden was stopped on Monday morning. The ferry operator said on its website it had taken the decision “to guarantee safety”.

The Rheden ferry, which takes pedestrians and cyclists across the IJssel at Rhederlaag, ran its last service on Monday evening.

Helmsman Richard van Oijen told Omroep Gelderland it was an unprecedented step. “We’ve been out of service in the past, but it was always because of high water.

“This is the first time I can remember not being able to run because of low water.”

Uitwaarde, which runs 10 connecting ferries in Gelderland, has suspended three of its routes across the Waal and Linge rivers because of low water.

The Rhine last week dropped to 6.46m, its lowest level, above sea level at Lobith, the point where the river enters the Netherlands from Germany. This week it is expected to fall another 11 centimetres.

River barges

The flow in the river is down to around one-third of its regular level for July, causing problems for cargo barges and river cruises. Several cruise operators have had to cancel or shorten trips upriver because the water is too low.

Restrictions have also been imposed on river barges, while nearer the river mouth sluice gates have been closed or limited to a few openings a day to prevent sea water getting into the drinking water supply.

The canal locks at Eefde, which up to 20,000 ships pass through a year between the IJssel river and the Twentekanaal, were closed for the first time last Friday, closing off traffic to Almelo, Hengelo and Enschede.

Deventer closed its harbour to shipping for the first time in eight years last week after the IJssel dropped below safe levels.

item.title: Police suspect three explosions in Assen in a week are linked
item.description:
Police suspect three explosions in Assen in a week are linked

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have stepped up security outside a house in Assen that has been hit by two explosions in a week.

The third blast was at around midnight on Saturday to Sunday, at the back of the house on Entingestraat, on the northern edge of the Drenthe capital. Nobody was injured.

The first explosion was outside the front of the house in the early hours of Tuesday, two days after another incident the previous weekend in Klaverstraat, on the eastern side of the town.

Police have placed cameras on poles outside both addresses and are investigating if the explosions are linked. They have appealed for witnesses or anyone with camera footage from the area to contact them on the non-emergency number 0900 8844.

item.title: Police arrest two after Amsterdam war memorial defaced
item.description:
Police arrest two after Amsterdam war memorial defaced

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Two men have been arrested after the national war memorial on the Dam in central Amsterdam was defaced early on Sunday morning.

Texts were sprayed on the monument in yellow and blue paint at around 5.15am, including a skull. Police said they have not yet established a motive.

A 27-year-old man from Hoofddorp was detained after a patrol car happened to pass through the square while he was using a spray can, a police spokesperson said. A 39-year-old Polish man was caught shortly afterwards writing on the back of the monument in lipstick.

Police could not say whether the two knew each other. The monument was cordoned off with tape while cleaners removed the paint.

Mayor Femke Halsema wrote on social media that it was appalling that the monument had been targeted again, and praised officers for making immediate arrests.

The memorial, unveiled in 1956, commemorates the Dutch war dead and is the site of the annual Remembrance Day ceremony on May 4. It was sprayed with red paint hours before this year’s ceremony, and daubed during a pro-Palestinian demonstration in 2025.

A court found the man responsible for the 2025 incident guilty last month but imposed no punishment, ruling that defacing the memorial was socially unacceptable and disproportionate whatever the political message behind it.

item.title: Trains cancelled after dog runs on to track near The Hague
item.description:
Trains cancelled after dog runs on to track near The Hague

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Train services between The Hague and Delft were suspended on Monday after a dog ran onto the track.

The disruptions began at 8am when a train had to stop to avoid hitting the animal. All main line services have been cancelled until at least 10.30am, including Intercity trains from Hollands Spoor station to Breda and Sprinter trains between The Hague and Dordrecht.

Trams between The Hague and Delft are running as normal. Passengers are advised to check the NS travel planner before setting out.

The setback happened just as services between The Hague and Utrecht resumed following work to repair a broken overhead power line.

NS said the cable was damaged by a train passing through Gouda on Sunday afternoon. The stranded train had to be led away before the power lines could be fixed. Replacement buses were laid on to transport passengers between Gouda and Lansingerland-Zoetermeer.

item.title: Jetten becomes first Dutch PM to join Pride canal parade
item.description:
Jetten becomes first Dutch PM to join Pride canal parade

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Rob Jetten became the first serving Dutch prime minister to take part in Amsterdam’s Pride canal parade on Saturday, joining a boat at the Scheepvaartmuseum and sailing part of the route through the city centre.

He used his appearance to announce that the cabinet would implement the Regenboog Stembusakkoord, a set of pledges on LGBTQI+ rights signed by seven parties last October.

Jetten also said new laws will be coming to strengthen the position of LGBTQI+ people, and that the cabinet was setting aside €35 million for safety measures and work with the police and the big cities.

The agreement was drawn up by the rights organisation COC and signed in October 2025 by all three parties now in the coalition government.

Its commitments include raising the number of police discrimination detectives from four to at least 40 and reviving a bill easing legal gender change that was withdrawn under the previous cabinet.

Jetten, who is openly gay, said in February that he receives constant threats over his sexuality. He encouraged young LGBTQI+ people to be open about who they are, saying it remained difficult in the Netherlands in 2026.

Eighty boats, tighter security
Around 80 boats sailed from the Oosterdok along the Nieuwe Herengracht and the Amstel to the Prinsengracht, where temporary stands had been built for WorldPride. Organisers gave no visitor figure but described the crowds as very busy.

The city council’s boat marked 25 years since the Netherlands became the first country to open civil marriage to same-sex couples.

Security was tightened after the attack on a Pride event in Berlin the previous week, with 250 concrete blocks placed along the canals. Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema said the city had prepared thoroughly but did not specify what the extra measures were.

The parade was the midpoint of WorldPride, which runs until August 8. The UNITY Concert takes place on Museumplein on Tuesday, followed by a human rights conference at the Beurs van Berlage, a mass wedding celebration on August 6 and a closing concert on August 8.

item.title: AZ hit four past 10-man PSV in emphatic Johan Cruyff Shield win
item.description:
AZ hit four past 10-man PSV in emphatic Johan Cruyff Shield win

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Cup winners AZ Alkmaar scored a resounding 4-0 win over PSV in the Johan Cruyff Shield, the traditional curtain-raiser to the Dutch league season.

The champions never recovered after Joey Veerman was sent off in the ninth minutes for raising his boot into the face of Mexx Meerdink.

Referee Serdar Gözübüyük appeared to be reaching for the yellow card at first, but showed the midfielder a straight red after consulting the VAR team.

It took until the 25th minute for AZ to force the breakthrought, as Meerdink, now sporting a scar behind his left ear, headed in from close range after PSV defender Ryan Flamingo deflected a cross into his path.

AZ wrapped up the match with two quick goals after half-time. Weslley Patati’s precise shot put daylight between the teams before Ro-Zangelo Daal cut open PSV’s defence with a pass to the unmarked Elijah Dijkstra, who stroked the ball into the net.

Daal completed the rout from the penalty spot in the 65th minute, while PSV were restricted to a couple of shots by Dennis Man and Guus Til that drew good saves from AZ goalkeeper Jari de Busser.

Meerdink “panic”

Veerman put up no protest against his red card, his first in 359 matches for PSV, but insisted that it was clumsy rather than malicious. “I felt bad for Mexx because he was lying trembling on the pitch. He had a big cut behind his ear.”

Meerdink said: “I thought my ear had come off. I was starting to panic. I don’t think Joey could have done much about it, but it’s dangerous play so it was a red card.”

PSV coach Peter Bosz said the dismissal of Veerman made it hard to assess the quality of his team, but still struck a positive note in his post-match press conference.

“It meant we could practice defending with a low block, something we usually only get to do in the Champions League,” he said.

item.title: Nationwide heat warning as temperatures set to reach 36°
item.description:
Nationwide heat warning as temperatures set to reach 36°

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The national heat plan has been extended to the whole of the Netherlands from Monday, with maximum temperatures forecast to reach 36° in the south.

Despite its name, the plan is a warning rather than a set of measures. It carries no legal force and requires nothing to close or stop.

The public health institute RIVM uses it to tell care organisations, health professionals and family carers that hot weather is coming, so they can adjust the support they give to elderly and vulnerable people.

RIVM activated the plan on 29 July for Limburg, Noord-Brabant, Gelderland and Overijssel and has not stood it down since. It is the third activation of the year, after extreme heat in June and July.

Code yellow until Tuesday
The KNMI weather service has issued a code yellow warning for heat running until midnight on Tuesday.

Monday will be sunny and dry, with highs ranging from 28° on the Wadden Islands to 36° in places in the south. A shower or thunderstorm is possible in the southeast in the evening.

The night into Tuesday will stay warm, with temperatures in the larger cities not dropping far below 20°.

Tuesday will reach 30° to 33° by early afternoon, warmest in the southeast and east, before cooling from the west. Thunderstorms are likely in the east of the country.

RIVM advises people to check on vulnerable neighbours and relatives, encourage them to drink more than usual, keep homes cool with blinds or fans, and move errands to before midday or after 6pm.

The heat should ease from Wednesday, with a maximum of 27° forecast, followed by 23° on Thursday and 22° on Friday.

item.title: “Amsterdam’s gay tourism scene doesn’t stretch beyond the city”
item.description:
“Amsterdam’s gay tourism scene doesn’t stretch beyond the city”

August 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

For over two decades, Michiel Hoogkamer has single-handedly managed Leiden’s sole gay bar. As it approaches its final weeks in business, he and others speak to Brandon Hartley about the challenges facing the country’s ‘homohoreca’ [gay nightlife scene].

Michiel Hoogkamer, the owner of De Roze Beurs, Leiden’s only gay bar, is ready
to call it quits.

After 24 years of catering for everyone from introverted university students to boisterous drag queens, the final night has been set for 15 August.

There’s no single reason why Hoogkamer decided to close down the bar he lovingly described as his child during an interview with Dutch News, but it comes at a difficult time for LGBTI+ oriented businesses all across the Netherlands.

While De Roze Beurs continues to host a stream of regulars, similar businesses across the country have struggled over the past decade.

“Here in the Netherlands, little bars like this one aren’t doing well,” Hoogkamer said. “Young people aren’t loyal to one place anymore. They go to monthly or quarterly parties at nightclubs instead or go to restaurants in the middle of the day.”

Hoogkamer and others say the country’s homohoreca is facing an increasing number of challenges.

Homohoreca is a Dutch term for hospitality businesses that cater for a gay, lesbian, transgender, and bisexual clientele, such as bars, saunas, nightclubs, and restaurants.

Saunas disappearing

Even Amsterdam is not immune. Cafe Getto, a popular gay-oriented restaurant that became famous for its ‘Diva Burgers,’ closed down a few years ago.

Lola the Green Aardvark, a queer food bar, and the lesbian/bisexual/queer café B’Femme both shuttered in 2025.

“The decline is drastic among gay saunas,” Peter Koop told Dutch News. “In 2020, there were still 12 gay saunas, but only eight remain.

“The closed saunas have not found successors. This is likely because there is hardly any interest in such establishments among young people anymore.”

Koop is the current writer and editor of homohoreca.nl, a website that has been tracking the industry since 2001.

However, a precise forecast of what’s to come could prove more difficult than predicting the weather in April.

“Although we do not have hard figures, we also have the impression that there are fewer bars and clubs aimed at the LGBTI+ community,” Philip Tijsma, spokesperson for the national LGBTQ+ rights group COC Nederland, said.

Changing habits

Many clientele are less reliant on these businesses to serve as safe spaces or
dating venues.

“We also have the impression that people’s nightlife behaviour has changed,’ Tijsma said.

“People go to a bar or club less often, and are more likely to attend a large LGBTI+ party or festival a few times a year. General nightlife venues have also sometimes become more inclusive and LGBTI+ people feel at home there more often.”

“In the Netherlands, there is indeed a decline in the number of gay bars, but that decline is very slow,” Koop said.

He said an average of two close in the Netherlands every year, but at least one new one usually appears.

Gay tourism

Koop also noted that, despite a downturn between 2010 and 2015, the number in Amsterdam has been holding steady.

“Amsterdam’s gay establishments benefit from gay tourism, which is not the case in the rest of the Netherlands,” he said.

The decrease is less severe than many people think, but the blow can be hard locally, as is the case with Leiden.”

The city still has a local chapter of COC Nederland but, aside from periodic club nights, it’s more of an advocacy centre than a social organisation.

Potential buyers

The building that houses De Roze Beurs has primarily served as a bar since it was built in 1636.

The name is somewhat difficult to translate into English, as beurs can mean various things such as stock exchange, marketplace and coin purse.

Hoogkamer said the name is partially a tribute to the years it was used as a meeting hall for officials and accountants from the Beestenmarkt, a nearby square where livestock was once sold.

He doesn’t know what the future holds for the building, but he doubts it will remain a gay bar.

A few interested parties have approached him about taking over De Roze Beurs, but the discussions didn’t go far. His landlord will make the ultimate decision about what happens next.

Homophobia increasing

Additional challenges new owners might face include what Hoogkamer says has been a rise in anti-gay hostility.

He said his first few years behind the bar could be rough at times. At one point in the early 2000s, the building was attacked by someone who threw paint bombs at the windows.

Things were largely quiet throughout the 2010s, but there’s been an uptick in aggression after De Roze Beurs reopened following the pandemic.

The rainbow flags out front have been stolen several times. On a busy Saturday night, a vandal smashed one of the windows and shouted anti-gay slurs at his customers.

Berlin attack

Hoogkamer also says there’s been an increase in passers-by heckling patrons seated outside on the terrace.

Recent studies suggest gay tolerance has declined in the Netherlands, especially among youths.

The Berlin Pride attack paints an even darker picture of the situation elsewhere
around the world.

“With the extreme right coming up, like Wilders and the FvD, it’s getting worse,” Hoogkamer said.

“They all say they’re woke and they’re attracting a lot of young people, but it simply isn’t true.”

Late nights

There’s also no denying that running any sort of bar can be incredibly difficult, especially once you enter middle age.

De Roze Beurs is essentially a one-man operation. “It’s hard work and I sometimes have 80-hour working weeks,” Hoogkamer said. “As you get older, you start to feel it, and there’s the long nights.

“I don’t get to bed until four or five in the morning. Everybody else gets to go home and I have to stay here and clean the toilets.”

When Dutch News recently visited De Roze Beurs, many of the rubber ducks that once stood watch over the bar itself had been packed up and placed into bags with other memorabilia.

Stripper pole

Along with an iconic stripper pole and pretty much everything else, the ducks will be sold at an auction scheduled for 20 August hosted by local drag queen Christine Carrington.

Hoogkamer will be sad to see it all go, but he said he was ready to move on.
“I’m going on sabbatical for a year,” he said. “I’m 46, I have good legs, and I want to see something of the world after managing a bar for so many years.”

While he himself wouldn’t take over a gay bar nowadays, he said Leiden could still use one, especially if there’s a person out there who knows what they’re getting themselves into.

“There’s plenty of potential in this city for a gay or queer bar, but you have to work hard,” he advised. “You’re not going to get rich and your social life is forever on hold.

“You can’t go to parties and you can’t go to birthdays because they’re all on Fridays and Saturdays. When do you make your money? On Fridays and Saturdays.”

item.title: Dutch unions call 24-hour public transport strike on September 9
item.description:
Dutch unions call 24-hour public transport strike on September 9

July 31, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Public transport workers across the Netherlands are to stage a one-day strike on Wednesday, September 9, bringing buses, trains, trams and metro services almost to a standstill.

The FNV union has called the strike in the latest escalation of its campaign against the government’s social welfare reforms, which it says will lead to lower living standards for millions of working people.

The three major unions FNV, CNV and VCP have vowed to fight the cabinet’s social welfare reforms, which are designed to secure €6.5 billion in cost savings during the goverment’s four-year term.

Social affairs minister Hans Vijlbrief scrapped a plan to increase the statutory retirement age faster by raising it in step with life expectancy, but the unions want the cabinet to go further by abandoning cuts to unemployment pay and long-term disability benefits.

Staff working for NS, ProRail, urban and regional transport sevices and DB cargo will down tools for 24 hours on September 9, making it impossible to run timetables.

Delays inevitable

“We are aware that a 24-hour strike will cause disruption,” said FNV official Edwim Kuiper. “We regret that deeply. But the consequences of the dismantling of our social security are much greater for everyone and will last much longer.”

National train operator NS said it could not say exactly what the impact of the stoppage would be because it had not been officially notified by the union.

Lobby organisation OV-NL, which represents nine smaller public transport companies such as Arriva, QBuzz and the major city network operators GVB, RET and HTM, said it “understood up to a point” the reason to call a strike.

But it said it was “very unfortunate that passengers are being disadvantaged by a social and political debate”.

Union leader Henri Janssen said that the strike was being called on behalf of commuters. “Every working person has to deal with sickness, work incapacity or involuntary unemployment. They should be able to count on a decent social safety net,“ he said.
